headlines.summary: JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, with mixed results.
headlines.article_text: Bank earnings October 2026: JPMorgan, Goldman, Wells Fargo, Citigroup Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Four of the largest U.S. banks reported third-quarter results on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase , Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs and Citigroup . Bank of America and Morgan Stanley will post earnings on Wednesday. The quarter was dominated by headlines around artificial intelligence, IPO uncertainty, high fuel prices and rising borrowing costs. The banks that reported Tuesday put up mixed results . JPMorgan, the biggest U.S. bank by assets and the largest in the world by market capitalization, posted a rare miss. Goldman Sachs, meanwhile, blew past estimates for revenue and earnings per share, led by strong equities trading. Analyst calls for all four banks touched on the opportunities and risks associated with AI, citing robust financing demand and operational advantages, but also the threat of rogue agents. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon also addressed recent reports of a CEO transition plan, and Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo joined CNBC to discuss the firm's growth and the state of the consumer. Here's what you need to know: JPM posts a rare earnings miss WFC is out with mixed results GS reports a massive revenue beat Citi's earnings report caps off the morning JPMorgan's CFO says deals are being 'delayed' Dimon says AI will 'benefit mankind enormously' Goldman CEO Solomon denies succession plans are in motion Wells Fargo CFO joins CNBC to discuss momentum and the consumer 6 Min Ago Citi call wraps, concluding Tuesday morning's reports Citi's analyst call is over, which means bank earnings reports for Tuesday are wrapped. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley report on Wednesday to round out third-quarter results for the major U.S. firms. — Sara Salinas 34 Min Ago Wells Fargo CFO says consumer is doing well watch now VIDEO 5:04 05:04 Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo: Consumer is doing well Squawk on the Street Wells Fargo's Santomassimo told CNBC that both consumers and businesses are doing "really well." "I think despite higher gas prices, both sides of the equation have been able to really work through that," he said. "We're just not seeing any sort of cracks around delinquency trends that would lead you to believe you're going to see any near-term stress that come through, at least at least for now." – Laya Neelakandan 38 Min Ago Wells Fargo CFO to CNBC: Momentum is growing Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo told CNBC's Sara Eisen that the company's underlying results are "really good" and that the bank is seeing "continued momentum" across all of its businesses. "As you look at the net interest margin, what that really shows is sort of this good stabilization of the underlying trends," he said. "You see the higher rate environment starting to come through in terms of helping it as you look forward, and so for us, the opportunity we have ahead of us is just as big as it was last quarter." VIDEO 6:23 06:23 Watch CNBC’s full interview with Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo – Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago Citi sees consumer continuing to drive growth Jane Fraser, chief executive officer of Citigroup Inc., during a Bloomberg Television interview on the sidelines of the Citi China Conference in Shanghai, China, on Friday, Nov. 14, 2025. Qilai Shen | Bloomberg | Getty Images Citi's Fraser said on the call with analysts that macro environment conditions softened during the third quarter and that the "global economy has held up remarkably well." "In the U.S., while much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much of the growth," she said. "The labor market is stable, and companies remain active. Our near-term economic outlook remains positive." She added that the bank's clients have remained "engaged" and "healthy." – Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago Citi CEO: Cyberdefense is a priority Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said on a call with analysts on Tuesday that the company is focused on reducing systemic risk while deploying AI firm-wide. "Our cyberdefense strategy is about being on the front foot, about moving fast and retaining trust," Fraser said. "We don't wait for risks to happen. We're constantly preparing and improving our defenses. We're in the business of managing risk everyday, and this is no different." – Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago Investment banking fees mostly hold up watch now VIDEO 3:52 03:52 Goldman Sachs CEO says IPO market was 'a little bit softer in September' Squawk on the Street Investment banking fees at all four firms reporting on Tuesday largely held up during the third quarter, with most firms either matching or surpassing prior guidance. Still, the reports revealed declines on a quarter-over-quarter basis. At JPMorgan, investment banking revenue was up 14% year over year but down 8% quarter over quarter. JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said the pipeline remains "very, very strong." Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon echoed that sentiment on his company's analyst call, while declining to say whether capital markets activity has peaked. That bank reported fees that were 21% higher from the prior year, but 5% lower than the second quarter. "IPOs that came in September were really the result of conversations in May and June around valuation expectations. Things got a little bit softer in September," Solomon said. "The IPO market was wide open. It's just if you expected a valuation and you got something 10 %to 15% less, you might choose not to go forward, you might choose to wait." Solomon added all the tech innovation and the AI infrastructure activity is a "real good ballast" for capital markets activity on a go-forward basis, noting that doesn't mean there won't be bumps. Citi posted the largest quarter-over-quarter decline in the fees, at 13% down. Wells Fargo reported investment banking revenue that was down 5% from the prior quarter. — Leslie Picker 2 Hours Ago Goldman Sachs CEO sees growing risks in financing the AI infrastructure buildout Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon speaks at the Economic Club of New York in New York City, on June 2, 2026. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Solomon warned that the AI infrastructure boom could face a painful reset if higher borrowing costs or overbuilding undermine the economics of some data center projects. "There is going to be a lot of financing to do, and we're going to be in the middle of that," Solomon said during the bank's third-quarter call. "It may be that over time as the financing needs grow, that there's pressure on rates and that will affect the returns and the viability of certain projects," he said. "Not every project is going to be received as well." For now, demand for computing power remains strong and supply has yet to catch up, Solomon said, meaning more infrastructure will be built and more financing from Goldman and others will be needed. It's impossible to predict when a reset might happen or how the technology would evolve and be deployed, he said, calling the dynamic "an unknown we have to live with." "There will be a point in time when this recalibration resets, for sure," Solomon said. "When that does happen, of course there'll be some bumps." — Hugh Son 2 Hours Ago Citigroup is beginning its conference call with analysts Citigroup, the final bank of the morning, is beginning its conference call with executives and analysts to discuss its third-quarter earnings results. – Laya Neelakandan 2 Hours Ago Goldman CEO David Solomon denies succession plans are in motion John Waldron, chief operating officer of Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon. Jason Alden | Bloomberg | Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Goldman Sachs CEO Solomon pushed back against reports of an impending transition to executive chairman, saying Tuesday that no succession process or timeline is underway at the investment bank. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: AAPL, META, BMBL, FRMI, GS Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Apple — The consumer technology giant gained 1% after unveiling its HomeView smart home hub . This device, powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, is designed for multiple people in a household and will use facial recognition to display pertinent information. Meta Platforms – Shares of the social media giant climbed more than 2%, rising for a second day following the rollout of its Muse Wonder artificial intelligence model. The release was well received by Wall Street, with Truist hiking its price target to $1,000 from $763. Bumble — The maker of the dating app saw shares soar 56% after announcing that it will be acquired by Ithaca Holdings in an all-cash deal valuing the company at $1.3 billion. Memory chip stocks — The group fell following a downbeat overnight session in South Korea. Concerns over memory stock valuations grew on the heels of CXMT's plans to roll out a new, more powerful chip by the end of 2026. U.S.-listed shares of SK hynix slid 4%, while Western Digital and Seagate declined 2%. Micron shed 4.9%, and Sandisk declined by 2.7%. AI infrastructure plays – A swath of artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks slid on Tuesday, tumbling alongside memory chip stocks. Applied Materials dropped 6%, while Lam Research and Teradyne each lost more than 3%. Lumentum fell more than 2%, and the iShares AI Innovation and Tech ETF (BAI) shed nearly 3%. Fermi – The developer of electric grids jumped 17% after signing a credit support agreement with Advanced Micro Devices , backing the first phase of Fermi's Project Matador energy and AI buildout in Texas. The companies have also signed a deal outlining a partnership as well as a framework to expand up to 650 megawatts of gross power capacity. JPMorgan Chase — Shares were marginally higher after the bank raised its net interest income outlook for the year. Gains were kept in check after the company reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that missed analyst expectations . Wells Fargo — The bank stock fell 1% on mixed Q3 results. Earnings per share of $1.87 exceeded an LSEG estimate of $1.85. Revenue of $21.87 billion was below a $22.3 billion forecast. Goldman Sachs — Shares rose nearly 1% after the banking giant reported Q3 revenue of $18.68 billion, exceeding an LSEG estimate of $16.71 billion. Johnson & Johnson — The pharma giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter, but soft medical device sales outweighed the earnings beat. MedTech revenue came in at $8.64 billion, falling short of the StreetAccount consensus call for $8.74 billion. Shares slid more than 6%. Domino's Pizza — The pizza chain fell 3% after its third-quarter results failed to impress investors. While earnings per share and revenue exceeded analyst estimates, U.S. same-store sales rose 0.3% — only in line with a FactSet consensus. Syndax Pharmaceuticals — Shares tumbled 16% after the company said axatilimab did not meet its primary endpoint during a Phase 2 trial in which the antibody was used to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. "The MAXPIRe trial did not meet its primary endpoint, and we are disappointed by this outcome given the promising scientific rationale in IPF," Nick Botwood, head of research & development at Syndax, said in a statement. Six Flags — The amusement park stock plunged 16% after a man died and others were injured in a roller coaster incident in Georgia, according to Cobb County police. UnitedHealth — The health insurance giant posted third-quarter results that beat analyst expectations. UnitedHealth earned an adjusted $4.69 per share on revenue of $112.69 billion. Analysts estimated a profit of $4.14 per share on revenue of $111.40 billion, according to LSEG. Shares were last up less than 1%. — CNBC's Nick Wells contributed reporting.

headlines.article_text: Boeing delivers 57 jets in September, highest monthly total for year Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A Boeing Co. 737 Max airplane at the company's manufacturing facility in Renton, Washington, US, on Thursday, Nov. 20, 2025. David Ryder | Bloomberg | Getty Images Boeing said on Tuesday that it delivered 57 jets in September, up from 51 in August and 55 a year earlier as it works to ramp up production of its best-selling 737 MAX narrow-body. It was the planemaker's highest monthly total so far this year. Turkish Airlines' order for 100 737 MAX jets boosted Boeing's September total of new orders to 165. The US planemaker still trailed European rival Airbus' 72 deliveries in September, but Boeing far outsold its rival, which booked only 17 new orders from two customers last month. Boeing's September deliveries included 43 737 MAX jets, eight 787s, two 777 freighters and four 767s, including three for Boeing's defense unit for completion as KC-46 aerial refueling tankers. The higher deliveries come as Boeing works to consistently increase 737 MAX output to 47 jets a month, which has taken longer than expected, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said during an investor conference in September. Through September, Boeing has delivered 475 jets this year, up 8% from a year earlier. That includes 363 737 MAX jets, the most the MAX program has ever delivered in the first nine months of a year. In addition to Turkish Airlines' order, Boeing booked orders for 20 737 MAX jets for Lufthansa, six 737 MAX and five 787 jets for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, and eight 777-8 freighters and two 777 freighters for Ethiopian Airlines. Another six 737 MAX and 18 787 orders came from unidentified customers. Boeing ended September with an official backlog of 6,371 jets, up from 6,156 at the end of August. headlines.article_text: Apple releases HomeView smart home hub to showcase Siri AI Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced the new HomeView that starts at $299. The iPhone maker also announced the new Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini. HomeView will act as a voice-controlled smart home hub for Apple devices and was built to showcase new Siri AI abilities. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT John Ternus, chief executive officer of Apple Inc., during a product unveiling event at Apple Park in Cupertino, California, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Apple on Tuesday announced a new home hub called HomeView . Apple said the device with a 7-inch screen was designed to be mounted on a wall or placed on a table. It's designed for multiple people in a household, and will recognize the user by their face to display pertinent information. It starts at $299 and ships on Nov. 13. Tuesday's launch event is the second under new CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September. Last month, Apple announced new models of its most important product, the iPhone, including a foldable model called the Duo that retails for nearly $2,000. Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday. The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and has a redesigned remote that can play a sound if it is lost. Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price. The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month. Apple said that HomeView features Siri AI, which can answer a broad range of questions. Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad. It has a built-in speaker for playing music. Apple's HomeView can be placed on a table or mounted on a wall. Apple "It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's chief marketer Greg Joswiak said in a statement. Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence. It can also be used to make FaceTime calls and as a digital photo frame. It's equipped with an Apple A18 chip. It supports up to six users. Apple TV, HomePods, and HomeView are included in Apple's Wearables, Home, and Accessories category, which reported $7.88 billion in sales in the most recent quarter ended June, which was about 7% of the company's total revenue. The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch. But while Apple has dabbled in home products and platforms in the past, Tuesday's announcement shows Apple is making its home products a higher priority under Ternus. The Apple HomeView, an iPad-like device meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops that will showcase its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant, during a launch of smart home products in New York City, US, October 13, 2026. Shannon Stapleton | Reuters Apple said on Tuesday that its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Apple's integration with the smart home is not just about sales but also helps further lock customers into its own ecosystem. People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone. HomeView can also become a smart home dashboard, Apple said. It can be used to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, or lock connected doors around the house. Apple said that setting up a new smart home device takes one tap from the user's iPhone. The next generation of the HomePod mini with support for Siri AI Apple Home Collection, part of Apple HomeView which includes an iPad-like device meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops that will showcase its AI-upgraded Siri virtual assistant, during a launch of smart home products in New York City, US, October 13, 2026. Shannon Stapleton | Reuters Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories. But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage. It also comes as new boss Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster. Apple's new Apple TV 4K got a price hike from $199 to $299, and comes after a similar price increase earlier this year, after Cook said that memory costs for Apple were unsustainable. headlines.title: J&J beats earnings estimates, eyes mid-2027 hip and knee unit spinoff
headlines.summary: Pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% in the quarter ⁠to $16.76 billion, but medical technology division sales rose just 2.5% to $8.6 billion.
headlines.article_text: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article JNJ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 8:52 08:52 Johnson & Johnson CFO Joseph Wolk on the company’s Q3 results Squawk Box Johnson & Johnson reported a slightly higher-than-expected profit on Tuesday, driven by strong sales of its immune disease treatment, Tremfya, and said it plans to spin off its hips-and-knees business next year. The company said late last year it intended to separate its orthopedics unit, DePuy Synthes, into a standalone company, marking its second major spinoff as it sharpens its focus on higher-growth healthcare segments. Chief Financial Officer Joe Wolk said on a conference call to discuss company results that J&J remains on track for a mid-2027 separation of DePuy Synthes. "Given the way DePuy Synthes is performing... we are leaning towards a spin as being the best option to create long-term value for Johnson & Johnson shareholders. That has always been our base plan, and we are confident that it can be successfully executed," he said. Apollo Global Management is in talks to acquire the orthopedics unit in a ​deal that could value it at close to $20 billion, Bloomberg News reported in September. J&J shares were off about 2% before the bell. Middle East conflict weighs on MedTech Wolk, in an interview, told Reuters the Middle East conflict, austerity measures in Europe and pricing in China continued to weigh on results internationally, "but maybe in a little bit more pronounced way." He said the Middle East conflict, which has driven up fuel costs, has not yet affected the company's costs but has hurt sales in the region. "These are countries that still value and actually want premium healthcare systems, think Kuwait, UAE, Saudi Arabia. They pride themselves on having solid healthcare, very good healthcare," Wolk said. "But their budgets now are being resourced and allocated towards defense." Medical technology division sales rose 2.5% to $8.6 billion overall, missing analysts' estimates of $8.71 billion, according to LSEG data. Outside the US, sales were essentially flat. The company raised its full-year sales forecast to about $101.2 billion at the midpoint, from $101.1 billion previously. It increased its adjusted earnings forecast range with a new midpoint of $11.10 per share, up from $11.04. Sales at J&J's Abiomed heart pump business remained slow after a UK study earlier this year raised questions about using Impella pumps in certain high-risk ​coronary procedures. The MedTech miss was largely in cardio and surgery, J.P. Morgan analyst Chris Schott said. Quarterly pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% to $16.76 billion. "While the results overall are generally in line with expectations, we believe investors will be disappointed in some of the details within the results," said Guggenheim analyst Vamil Divan, noting that the MedTech results were "somewhat disappointing." Divan pointed to strong sales of older products such as Stelara and Simponi, adding that Tremfya and Tecvayli, a multiple myeloma treatment, were the only newer, strategically important products that appear to have meaningfully beaten expectations. Tremfya sales for Crohn's disease and other autoimmune conditions rose 68% to $2.4 billion, beating analyst estimates of about $2.2 billion, while Stelara sales, which face generic competition, fell 54% to $716 million, still well above diminished Wall Street expectations of $591 million. Tremfya has increasingly replaced lost Stelara revenue following recent approvals in inflammatory bowel diseases. Sales of blood cancer treatment Darzalex rose about 16% to $4.24 billion, short of analysts' expectations of $4.4 billion. The company posted third-quarter revenue of $25.4 billion, above estimates of $25.28 billion, and adjusted earnings of $2.59 per share, topping Wall Street expectations by 5 cents. headlines.article_text: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points UnitedHealth Group posted third-quarter earnings that blew past estimates and raised its full-year profit outlook. The nation's largest private insurer continues to manage high medical costs and is seeing investments in value-based care and artificial intelligence take hold, CFO Wayne DeVeydt said in an interview. The company said it expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20 per share. In this article UNH Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT UnitedHealth Group signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange on April 21, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images UnitedHealth Group on Tuesday posted third-quarter earnings that blew past estimates and raised its full-year profit outlook, as the company continues to manage high medical costs and sees investments in value-based care and artificial intelligence take hold. The nation's largest private insurer said it expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20 per share. The healthcare giant's turnaround plan is gaining momentum after three consecutive strong quarters this year. UnitedHealth is working to stabilize margins by shrinking membership, exiting unprofitable contracts, and ramping up investments in artificial intelligence and value-based care, which tie doctor and facility compensation to patient health outcomes, quality of care and cost effectiveness rather than the volume of medical services provided. "You'll see in the quarter that we continue to execute not only on the financial aspects of our business, but really doing them with a simpler approach and an approach that's really focused on investing heavily in value-based care," CFO Wayne DeVeydt said in an interview. Here's what the company reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $4.69 adjusted vs. $4.14 expected Revenue: $112.69 billion vs. $111.40 billion expected The company posted third-quarter net income of $4.11 billion, or $4.56 per share, compared with $2.35 billion, or $2.59 per share, in the same period a year ago. Excluding items like business divestitures, restructuring and the expected reduction of reserves for unprofitable contracts, UnitedHealth earned $4.69 per share. Revenue fell to $112.69 billion from $113.16 billion a year earlier. The company's insurer, UnitedHealthcare, and its Optum healthcare unit both topped analysts' operating earnings estimates for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Managing high costs Notably, UnitedHealth's medical cost ratio — a measure of total medical expenses paid relative to premiums collected — came in at 88.4% for the third quarter. Analysts were expecting a ratio of 89.9%, according to StreetAccount. A lower ratio typically indicates the company collected more in premiums than it paid out in benefits, resulting in higher profitability. Still, DeVeydt told CNBC that medical costs in the quarter "continue to be elevated versus historical norms" — an issue that has plagued insurers, particularly those operating privately run Medicare Advantage plans, for more than two years. "I think it's something we should keep an eye on. I think you'll see that our medical care ratio has improved quite a bit, but I don't want that to be misleading in terms of [medical cost trends]," DeVeydt said. He said the independent dispute resolution, or IDR, process under the No Surprises Act is adding at least 100 basis points, or 1 percentage point, to total medical costs. That federal law, which took effect in 2022, aims to protect consumers from unexpected medical bills. The IDR process allows providers and insurers to resolve disputes over out-of-network payments. DeVeydt said those changes are driving up the company's claims costs, which can ultimately be passed on to consumers through higher premiums. DeVeydt added that costs for inpatient services and pharmacy, particularly costly specialty pharmacy drugs for cancer and rare diseases, remain elevated. Still, he highlighted the company's value-based care efforts, which he said are helping control medical costs by steering patients toward the right providers and emphasizing preventive care, DeVeydt added. He said acute hospital admissions among UnitedHealth members fell 15% year over year through the third quarter, while home health admissions rose 10%, suggesting more patients are receiving care in lower-cost settings. "You're finding more members are actually getting into a lower-cost care environment, but more importantly, they're getting into the care environment they actually want to be in," he told CNBC. "So we think we're really balancing both the quality and the cost." UnitedHealth is also rolling out AI-powered ambient listening tools to reduce physicians' administrative burden and free up time for patient visits. Appointment scheduling done by patients rather than with the assistance of a provider increased 27% year over year, DeVeydt said. He expects those initiatives to have a compounding effect on medical cost management through the fourth quarter and into 2027 as the programs expand.
